claim.pdf_says: D.2.2   File organization / D.2.2.1   Sequential organization  [printed page 1005] ... D.2.2.2   Relative organization  [printed page 1006]
claim.markdown_says: #### D.2.2 File organization / #### D.2.2.1 Sequential organization  (page-1035 slice) ... ## D.2.2.2 Relative organization  (page-1036 slice)
claim.why_it_matters: The markdown heading depth allegedly resets at every PDF page break instead of tracking the clause number, so D.2.2.2 is emitted at '##' - the same level as the '## Page 1036' scaffolding heading and two levels ABOVE its own parent D.2.2 ('####'). In any generated table of contents or heading-driven navigation, D.2.2.2 through D.2.2.5.3 detach from D.2.2 and read as peers of the annex itself. No normative text is lost (the clause number is preserved inline in the heading text), so this is structural, not normative. Claimed to be systemic: D.2.3.2.3 at '##' under D.2.3.2 at '###', D.2.4.3.1 at '##' vs sibling D.2.4.3.2 at '###', and a document-wide census of 2304 '##' / 1413 '###' / 96 '####'.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED. No heading is missing and no PDF content is lost, altered, or added. This is a markdown-formatting observation misfiled as a PDF-vs-markdown content discrepancy. Five independent grounds, each verified directly: (1) THE HEADING IS PRESENT, VERBATIM AND COMPLETE. I rendered spec_p1036.png at 300 dpi and read the glyphs. Printed page 1006 carries exactly one clause heading - bold serif 'D.2.2.2 Relative organization' - plus three body paragraphs ('A file with relative organization is a mass storage file...', 'Conceptually, a file with relative organization is a serial string of areas...', 'In order to achieve more efficient access to records in a relative file...'). The page-1036.md slice carries '## D.2.2.2 Relative organization' preceded by an explicit '' anchor, with all three paragraphs matching. specs/ISO_COBOL.md:41534 holds the same heading with clause number and title intact. The kind label 'missing-heading' is factually wrong - nothing is missing. (2) THE PDF ENCODES NO DEPTH FOR THE MARKDOWN TO LOSE - VERIFIED BY MY OWN READING OF THE GLYPHS, NOT INHERITED. I rendered page 1035 (printed 1005) specifically to test this. 'D.1 General', 'D.2 Files', 'D.2.1 General', 'D.2.2 File organization' and 'D.2.2.1 Sequential organization' are ALL set in the identical bold serif at the identical point size, with the identical left margin indent and identical spacing above and below. Page 1006's 'D.2.2.2 Relative organization' is set the same way. ISO varies no heading typography by clause depth anywhere in Annex D; depth is conveyed SOLELY by the dotted clause number, which the markdown preserves exactly. A '#' count is metadata the markdown layer invents - it cannot 'disagree with' a source that has no such attribute. (3) THE CLAIM'S CAUSAL STORY IS FALSE, INCLUDING ON THE VERY PAGE IT CITES. The depth is not a clause-depth mapping that 'resets at page breaks' - it is never a clause-depth mapping. On the page-1035 slice, with NO page break intervening, parent '#### D.2.2 File organization' (line 41514) is immediately followed by its own child '#### D.2.2.1 Sequential organization' (line 41517) at the SAME level. The identical parent/child level collision occurs in normative body text far from any annex: line 15910 '## 13.4 File section' and line 15959 '## 13.4.5 File description entry' - a child emitted at its parent's level - while 13.4.1 through 13.4.4 and 13.4.5.1 through 13.4.5.4 sit at '###'. Depth is a shallow slice-local rhythm clamped at 4; the page boundary is a coincidence, not the cause. There is consequently no hierarchy encoding for D.2.2.2 to 'detach' from. (4) THE STATED HARM DOES NOT MATERIALIZE - DEPTH IS NOT THE NAVIGATION MECHANISM. Every clause carries an explicit, stable, clause-derived anchor (''), and cross-references are '](#section-...)' links. The repo's own consumer of this file, scripts/spec/extract_rule_catalog.py, matches headings with HEADING = re.compile(r"^#{2,6}\s+(?P\d+(?:\.\d+)*)\s+(?P.+?)\s*$") - deliberately depth-agnostic across '##' through '######', deriving structure from the CAPTURED CLAUSE NUMBER rather than the '#' count. That same file already documents the per-page heading artifact as expected: 'PAGE-BREAK FURNITURE. At every printed page boundary the transcription injects a running header, and it is emitted AS A HEADING.' (5) THIS IS PAGE-BREAK FURNITURE BY THE RUBRIC'S OWN REJECT CRITERION, AND THE SUPPORTING CENSUS IS INFLATED. The level change coincides exactly with the '---' + '<a id="page-1036"></a>' + '## Page 1036' + '# ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' scaffolding block - content the transcription inserts and the PDF does not contain (note the running header lands at '#', level 1, ABOVE the page heading). Re-running the census: 2304 '##' / 1413 '###' / 96 '####' are correct raw counts, but 1233 of the 2304 '##' lines are '## Page NNNN' scaffolding, leaving only ~1071 actual '##' clause headings. The claim cites the inflated 2304 as evidence of a page-local reset; more than half of that number is the furniture itself and says nothing about clause depth. (The claim's related figure of 1261 is the '<a id="page-' anchor count, not the '## Page' heading count.) The two sibling examples cited (D.2.3.2.3 at '##' under D.2.3.2 at '###'; D.2.4.3.1 at '##' vs D.2.4.3.2 at '###') do check out in the file, so the underlying observation that markdown heading depth is inconsistent is TRUE - it is simply not a discrepancy against the PDF, and not page-break-driven. If the project wants clause-number-driven heading depth for ToC generation, that is a transcription-tooling enhancement to raise once against the whole document, on its own terms. It must not enter the reconciliation ledger as lost or altered spec content.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a PDF-vs-markdown discrepancy. Heading 'D.2.2.2 Relative organization' is transcribed completely and verbatim from printed page 1006, clause number intact, with a '' anchor, and all three body paragraphs match glyph-for-glyph; nothing is missing, so the 'missing-heading' kind is wrong. I rendered page 1005 and confirmed the PDF sets every Annex D clause heading (D.1, D.2, D.2.1, D.2.2, D.2.2.1) and page 1006's D.2.2.2 in the same bold serif at the same size and indent - the source encodes no heading depth for the transcription to lose, since depth lives only in the dotted clause number, which is preserved. The observed markdown '#'-depth inconsistency is real but internal to the markdown and is NOT page-break-driven as claimed: parent D.2.2 and child D.2.2.1 are both '####' on the same page with no break between them, and the same parent/child collision occurs in normative body text ('## 13.4 File section' at line 15910 vs its child '## 13.4.5 File description entry' at line 15959). The supporting census is inflated - 1233 of the 2304 '##' lines are '## Page NNNN' scaffolding. The stated navigation harm does not arise: consumers address clauses by stable '#section-...' anchors, and scripts/spec/extract_rule_catalog.py matches '^#{2,6}' deliberately, deriving structure from the captured clause number. Route as an optional transcription-tooling improvement (derive heading level from the clause number), not as a spec-reconciliation finding.
